steps: Unpack + open the firebox

Free the safety barrier from the pallet (two screws; snap off the perforated strap sections). Lift off the top plate, remove the top convection shroud (four hex screws, 10 mm), unlatch the glass frame and take out the top plate insert and log set.

The stove is heavy, so have help. Enamelled parts can be damaged if handled without care; set removed parts on a towel.

  1. Safety barrier: it is secured to the shipping pallet. Remove two screws and break off the perforated shipping-strap sections from both screen frame brackets with pliers.
  2. Lift the top plate straight off.
  3. Remove four hex head screws (10 mm wrench) and lift off the top convection shroud. Pull both spring latch handles forward and lift the glass frame straight up and out.
  4. Remove the top plate insert and the log set package from the firebox.

Hardware bag: fuel conversion kit - LP 157865, ember stones (1 oz.), top plate insert for rear exit applications. The manual suggests installing the optional blower now, before the stove goes to its final location, for easy access (see the blower note in the gas step).
Rear-exit conversion (if used)

Built for top exit. For rear exit, unbolt the vent adaptor (4 collar + 10 perimeter screws, 1/4" nut driver), move the exhaust cover plate to the top outlet, refit the adaptor facing rear and set the top plate insert in the top plate cut-out.

1. With a 1/4" nut driver, remove the 4 inner collar screws, then five screws from the top perimeter and five from the rear perimeter. The vent adaptor comes away as an assembly.
  2. Remove the four screws on the rear exhaust cover plate and re-install the plate over the top outlet.
  3. Turn the adaptor outlet to the rear and secure it with the same screws.
  4. Once the top convection shroud and top plate are back on, set the cast iron top plate insert in the top plate outlet cut-out.

Glass frame back in (after all accessories)

Press one of the two tabs under the stove to open the lower channel of the glass frame retainer, press the frame down until fully seated, then engage both spring latches.
Site the stove

Keep the minimum clearances from the stove body (rear 1 1/2", sides and corner 2", ceiling 20.25") and use floor protection on any combustible floor other than wood. Mantel clearances are lettered drawings on p. 9.

Plan for heat distribution, vent termination, gas line routing, and traffic areas, furniture and draperies, with access around the stove for service.

Rear (from rear shroud)1 1/2" (38 mm)
Sides / corner (from top plate)2" (51 mm)
Ceiling (from top plate)20.25" (514 mm)
Alcove24" max deep · 32 1/2" min wide

"Fire resistant" materials and fire-rated sheet rock count as combustible. The safety barrier has no effect on clearances.

Mobile homes (p. 29)

Approved in the U.S. and Canada if the stove is secured to the floor (Floor Bracket Kit #750304), an electrical ground is made between the stove and the chassis, and it is installed to Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 (U.S.) or CSA Z240.4 (Canada).
Vent system + restrictor

Use one approved vent maker's parts only and seal each inner-pipe joint with a 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac (no silicone). Terminate inside a zone of the vent matrix and set the exhaust restrictor dial to match.

• Approved systems: M&G DuraVent DirectVent Pro and GS Series, American Metal Products (Amerivent), Security Chimneys (Secure Vent), Selkirk Metalbestos (Direct Temp), Metal-Fab (Sure-Seal Direct Vent), Industrial Chimney (ExcelDirect), Bernard Dalsin (Pro Form), Olympia Chimney Supply (Ventis Direct Vent). Never mix makers in one system.
  • Its own vent only: never a chimney serving a solid fuel or gas appliance; common vent systems are prohibited.
  • Vertical: no cap discharge opening less than 18 in. (457 mm) from any roof surface or wall; a firestop at every floor; enclose venting exposed in living space above the first floor; wall straps every three feet on offsets.
  • Horizontal cap: 3" to overhead combustible projections of 2 1/2" or less, 12" to deeper ones; a vinyl siding standoff on vinyl or irregular siding; never recessed into the wall or siding.

Co-linear (masonry or Class A chimney)

3-inch co-linear flexible vent approved for a solid-fuel fireplace; 10 ft. min and 35 ft. max height; 24" max offset. The flue must first be cleaned and inspected by a qualified chimney service person. Masonry needs a fireclay liner the entire length; prefabricated chimneys must be UL 103 or ULC S-629 listed with a minimum inside diameter of 6 inches (150 mm). The air intake flex must extend 6 feet beyond the damper area; if it doesn't run the full length, a metal block off plate must seal the flue from the room.

Terminal clearances to windows, doors, corners, gas meters and air inlets (U.S. and Canada) are tabulated on p. 15.
Fuel conversion (if propane)

Ships for natural gas only. An authorized service technician fits the supplied kit 157865 before the stove is installed: pilot orifice, both burner injectors, the propane baffle change, the regulator tower and the labels.

1. Turn off the gas. Remove the top plate, top convection shroud and glass frame.
  2. Burner out: remove both air shutter wing nuts, washers and gaskets under the firebox; lift out the two panel support shelves; remove the burner bracket screws; pull the burner forward and up off the injectors.
  3. Pilot orifice: release the retainer clip, lift off the pilot head and swap the orifice with the 4 mm hex key (#51 NG, #30 LP).
  4. Injectors: 1/2" wrench; "L" = Left (rear), "R" = Right (front). Don't over-tighten; it can damage the brass elbow and cause a gas leak.
  5. Propane only: remove the baffle assembly (two 6 mm nuts), detach the secondary baffle (two sheet metal screws) and keep it, then refit the assembly.
  6. Refit the burner (two #8x1/2" screws), shelves, shutter gaskets, washers and wing nuts. Replace the regulator tower (Torx T-20).
  7. Labels: A on the back of the stove, B on the rating plate, the small label on the valve.
  8. Reassemble, leak-test with soapy water or a digital gas detector, check pressures with a manometer, then set the air shutters (LP 1/8" / NG 1/16" open to start).
Gas connection + leak test

Connect at the left side of the valve: 3/8" NPT with a 1/2" diameter supply, plus a shut-off valve (gas cock) and union in the same room (T-handle in Massachusetts). Leak-test every joint with 50-50 soapy water; never a flame.

• Size the supply to give enough pressure at the valve at any input setting.
  • Flexible gas appliance connectors are acceptable in many U.S. areas; Canadian methods vary with local code.
  • Propane: use propane-resistant sealing compounds.
  • Massachusetts: T-handle gas cock (248CMR), and installation by a licensed master or journeyman plumber or gas-fitter.
  • Leak test with the appliance lit: brush or spray every joint with a 50-50 water and dish soap solution. Bubbles or gas odor: turn the gas control knob to OFF, tighten or reconnect, retest.
Note: p. 19 says to install the optional blower before connecting the gas line, to prevent clearance interference between the two; p. 22 says to connect the gas supply line before installing the blower, using a 90° elbow off the control valve to create clearance for it.
Pressure test + high altitude

Manometer on test point A (inlet) and B (manifold) with the regulator control knob on HIGH. Above 2000 feet, check whether the gas supplier derates; if not, fit high altitude kit 157696 (NG) or 157695 (LP).

Inlet (A) natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Inlet (A) propane12.0 – 14.0 in. WC
Manifold (B) natural gas1.2 – 3.8 in. WC
Manifold (B) propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC

Disconnect the stove and its main gas valve from the supply piping for system tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut-off valve for tests at 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa) or less.

High altitude kit: follow the burner injector steps from the fuel conversion with the kit's injectors, leak- and pressure-test, run the system check and flame adjustment, then fill out the high altitude conversion label and apply it to the rating plate.
Accessories
Wall thermostat or remote receiver to the terminal block right of the main gas valve (750 millivolt DC two-wire, 16 gauge min, 25 feet max). Then the optional brick panels and blower.

Wall thermostat 750003 / remote 224910

Use only a 750 millivolt DC two-wire thermostat, in the same room, typically 5 feet off the floor and out of drafts. Minimum 16 gauge wire, maximum 25 feet, to either terminal of the block; no other wires need disconnecting; don't overtighten. The remote receiver wires the same way. For thermostat use, the On/Off/T-Stat switch on the back of the stove must be on T-stat and the pilot running (it powers the thermostat).

Brick panel kit 157697

Bend out the retainer tabs at the upper firebox corners, set the lower (smaller) panel on the rear shelf, the upper panel on it, then each side panel on its shelf under its tab; bend the tabs down.

Blower kit 156000

Snapstat bracket on the firebox-floor studs (two M6 hex nuts), blower bracket with two M6 flange head bolts, remove the air deflectors, blower ducts to the rear, wing screw, snapstat into its bracket slot, harness quick-connector, power cord to the nearest outlet, plugged directly into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle. Label all wires before servicing the controls.

Note: p. 19 says to install the optional blower before connecting the gas line, to prevent clearance interference between the two; p. 22 says to connect the gas supply line before installing the blower, using a 90° elbow off the control valve to create clearance for it.
Install the log set
Place the six logs in numbered order (#1 rear log on the rear-shelf pins, then #2 to #6), mating the holes to the pins. Spread ember stones sparsely and keep the pilot carry-over ports clear.

The log set must be in place before the burner is operated. Wear gloves and handle the logs carefully.

  1. #1 Rear Log onto the pins on the rear shelf; place 8 ember stones over the burner ports as shown in fig. 8.2.
  2. #2 Lower Left and #3 Lower Right onto the burner.
  3. #4 Upper Left, #5 Upper Right and #6 Small Front Log.
  4. Spread ember stones (#7) sparsely over the burner ports as shown; none over the ports at the rear log and pilot areas beyond those in fig. 8.2.

Exact positions are shown in figures 8.1-8.5. Complete log set: #158277.
System check + flame picture

With the glass frame off, purge the line, check the pilot, then time light-off on LOW: full burner ignition within 4 seconds cold, and again hot with the frame back on. Fine-tune the air shutters after 20-30 minutes on HIGH.

1. Purge: first lighting takes a few moments to clear air from the line. From a cold start, letting the pilot burn 10 - 15 minutes helps establish positive draft.
  2. Pilot (in the cut-out under the rear log): steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow at the edges; engulfing the thermocouple and thermopile and reaching the burner carry-over ports. Adjust with the screw to the right of the valve regulator knob.
  3. Regulator knob: flame height should change about 50% between LOW and HIGH. No smoke or soot; if present, check log placement, then the air shutters.
  4. Light-off on LOW: cold start, full ignition within 4 seconds. Reinstall the glass frame, run 5-10 minutes, off 2 minutes, then hot start, again within 4 seconds. Slower: see the Ceramic Burner Guide troubleshooting (not in this manual).
  5. Air shutters (qualified technician only): start at NG 1/16" (1.5 mm), LP 1/8" (3 mm); burn 20-30 minutes on HIGH; if the flame is weak, slow or sooty, open in 1/16" increments, letting it settle between changes; tighten the wing nuts.
Note: p. 26 says the right air shutter controls the rear burner and the left shutter the front burner; pp. 16, 18 and 32 list the burner injectors as left = rear and right = front.

panels.title: Sooty, yellow flame
items: Very long yellow flames, black soot on logs, firebox walls or the cap → air setting too small (incomplete combustion)
Smoke or soot → check log placement first; if it persists, adjust the air shutters
Weak, slow or sooty flame after 20-30 minutes on HIGH → open the shutter in 1/16" increments

panels.title: Blue, weak flame
items: Blue, transparent "anemic" flame → air setting too large
Poor combustion, weak flame picture → overly strong draft; set the exhaust restrictor for the termination zone
More offsets in the vent → greater need for air shutter adjustment

panels.title: Poor draft
items: Poor draft or draft reversal → steep roof, nearby trees, wind; a taller vent may help
Co-linear cold start problems → draft reversal; a return loop in the air intake run helps
No positive draft from a cold start → let the pilot burn 10 - 15 minutes before the burner

panels.title: Pilot & ignition
items: Pilot goes out when the knob is released → repeat lighting steps 5 through 7
Pilot won't stay lit after several tries, or the knob won't spring back → call a service technician or gas supplier
Full burner ignition over 4 seconds → Ceramic Burner Guide troubleshooting (not in this manual)

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
You light the pilot by hand with the red spark button. It then stays lit, and the burner switch (or a wall thermostat) turns the flames on and off.

First, smell all around the stove for gas, down by the floor too, since some gas is heavier than air. If you smell gas, don't light it. See Safety & gas smell.

  1. Set the burner switch to OFF, or the thermostat to its lowest setting.
  2. Check that the shut-off valve on the gas supply line is open.
  3. Push the control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF.
  4. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. If you smell gas now, stop.
  5. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counter-clockwise to PILOT.
  6. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the red spark button again and again until the pilot lights.
  7. Keep holding for about one minute, then let go. The knob should spring back and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, start again at step 4.
  8. Turn the knob counter-clockwise to ON.
  9. Set the burner switch to ON, or the thermostat to the temperature you want.
Call your service technician or gas supplier if the knob doesn't spring back, or the pilot won't stay lit after several tries (turn the knob to OFF first). Turn the knob by hand only, never with tools. If it won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

flame.title: Adjusting the flame
flame.html:
Two controls in the controls compartment set how much heat you get.

Regulator knob: flame height

Turn the regulator knob to raise or lower the flames. Flame height changes by about 50% between LOW and HIGH. This is the only control to use for adjusting flame height.

Front burner valve: on or off

A ball valve turns the front burner on or off, for more or less heat. Use it fully open or fully closed only. Never set it part way to dim the front flames.

Maker's website: Dual burner: Up to 70% heat control turn down.

What you should see

  • No smoke or soot. If you see either, the log placement should be checked. If it keeps happening, the air shutters may need adjusting.
  • Blue, see-through flames, or very long yellow flames that leave black soot, also point to the air setting.
  • The pilot, behind the burner under the rear log, should be steady: blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow at the edges.
Only a qualified, professional service technician should adjust the air shutters.

sounds.title: Sounds, smells and foggy glass
sounds.html:
Creaks and pings

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as the temperature changes. Creaking or pinging is that natural movement, not a fault.

A soft hum

The optional blower hums slightly on its low setting and gets louder as the fan speeds up.

Smoke or a smell at first

Some smoke and odor is normal during the first hours of use, while the metal and manufacturing materials cure under heat. It's temporary. Let plenty of fresh air move through the room.

Fog on the glass

Condensation can form on the glass each time you light the stove. It clears as the glass heats up.

After the first few fires a white powdery film shows up on the glass. Clean it off (see Clean the glass), or it can etch the glass for good.
A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, touch switches or use any phone in the building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
After the first few fires

A white powdery residue appears as the burner media cures. You need to clean it off: left on, it can permanently etch the glass. Use a non-abrasive household glass cleaner and warm water.

Everyday care

  • Clean the glass only when it needs it, and only when it's cool.
  • Wipe with a clean, damp, soft cloth, then dry with a soft towel.
  • Take care not to scratch it. Scratches weaken the glass, and a scratched panel should be replaced.
Never use abrasive or ammonia-based cleaners, and never clean the glass while it is hot.

Don't use the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Replacement glass should be fitted by a licensed or qualified service person, using only glass from your authorized Jøtul dealer.

Note: p. 28 says to use only Jøtul PN 225476 for replacement glass and names replacement glass kit 157710; the parts list on p. 33 gives Glass Panel, Ceramic 226734 and Replacement Glass Kit 158267.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
Everyday off

Set the burner switch to OFF. The flames go out, but the pilot stays lit, so the stove is ready for next time.

Complete shutdown

To shut off gas to the stove completely, push the valve control knob in and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it. After a complete shutdown, relight the pilot using the full lighting steps.

Before any cleaning or service, turn off the gas supply and disconnect power (unplug the optional blower).

The stove runs with a continuously burning pilot, so take care when using household products that give off combustible vapors.

thermostat.title: Wall thermostat & remote
thermostat.html:
Both are optional accessories that your installer wires to the stove's terminal block: a wall thermostat (750003) or an on/off remote control (224910).

Running on a thermostat

  • Set the On/Off/T-Stat switch on the back of the stove to T-Stat.
  • The pilot must be lit. It is the power source for the thermostat.
  • The thermostat belongs in the same room as the stove, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafts.

The remote

Follow the operating instructions that come with the remote control. They aren't part of this manual.

The stove can turn on suddenly. Set to run on a thermostat, it may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be on. Keep children away, keep the remote where children can't reach it, and stay clear of the burner when you use the remote.

blower.title: The optional blower
blower.html:
The optional variable-speed blower (kit 156000) moves more heat around the firebox and out into the room.

Automatic or manual

  • AUTO: a heat-activated switch (the snapstat) starts the fan once the stove has been burning for a while. When the burner turns off, the fan shuts off by itself as the stove cools down. The snapstat only works in AUTO.
  • MANUAL: choose this if you don't want automatic fan control.

The control switch also has an OFF position. Turn the speed control knob to set how fast the fan runs.

A slight hum on low, growing as the fan speeds up, is normal.

Power: the blower has a three-prong grounding plug. Plug it straight into a properly grounded three-prong outlet, never cut or remove the grounding prong, and unplug it before any service.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't light any appliance, touch any electrical switch, or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the stove

  • The surfaces get very hot. Everyone should stay away to avoid burns or clothing catching fire. Supervise young children in the room.
  • The barrier screen that came with the stove guards against burns from the hot glass. It must be in place before you use the stove, and put back after any service. If it's damaged, replace it with the Jøtul barrier for this stove (PN 157691).
  • Keep the stove away from furniture and drapes, and keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from it. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable liquids nearby.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane. Never burn wood, cardboard, paper or coal.
  • Don't slam or strike the glass.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

service.title: Annual service & care
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the stove and its venting before use and at least once a year.

Every year

  • The entire vent system, including the chimney, is inspected and cleaned.
  • A qualified technician inspects and cleans the pilot assembly and replaces any part showing corrosion.
  • The glass gasket is checked for wear and a positive seal.
  • The firebox and valve compartment are vacuumed with a soft brush attachment, handling the fragile logs carefully. Vacuum more often if you have pets.

Between services

  • Keep the control compartments and the area under the stove free of dust.
  • Every so often, check that nothing blocks the firebox, valve compartment, convection airways or blower. Lint from carpeting or bedding can mean cleaning more often.
Before any service, turn off the gas supply and disconnect power to the stove.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, steel burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas & electrical: controls, plumbing, valve, blower1 year

Good to know

  • It is void if installation or service is done by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier, or not to the manual and local or national codes.
  • Not covered: normal-wear parts such as paint, gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress), damage in transit, unauthorized changes, and enamel damage from misuse.
  • Contact your authorized Jøtul dealer, who processes claims. Jøtul must get notice of a possible defect within 60 days of finding it. Keep your dated sales receipt.
  • The warranty can't be transferred.
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC (1.25 – 1.74 kPa)
Propane12.0 – 14.0 in. WC (3.0 – 3.48 kPa)

Read at test point A on the front of the valve with the regulator control knob on HIGH. Supply connects at the left side of the valve: 3/8" NPT with a 1/2" diameter supply, or sized to hold pressure at any input setting. The tools list calls for an external regulator for propane.

Disconnect the stove for supply-piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); isolate it with its shut-off valve for tests at 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa) or less.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.2 – 3.8 in. WC (.30 – .95 kPa)
Propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC (.72 – 2.74 kPa)

Read at test point B with the regulator control knob on HIGH. The pilot adjustment screw sits to the right of the regulator knob. Recheck pressures with a manometer after any fuel conversion or high altitude change.

specRestrictor.title: Exhaust restrictor
specRestrictor.html:
An adjustable plate in the firebox exhaust outlet. It prevents an overly strong draft that can cause poor combustion and a weak flame picture.

Factory settingPosition A, fully open (no restriction)
Rangezero to approximately 70%
PositionsA, B, C = termination zones in the vent matrix
  1. Find the zone on the Vent Termination Zone Matrix (fig. 4.9, p. 11). Rise and run are measured from the stove top to the first discharge opening of the cap.
  2. Lift off the top plate and loosen the lock nut on the dial on top of the exhaust outlet (1/4" nut driver).
  3. Pivot the dial to the zone's position, tighten the lock nut and replace the top plate.

On a division line, use the less restrictive position: 10 feet high with a 7 feet offset is Position B. A 36" Snorkel normally needs no restriction (keep Position A).

The zone matrix is a diagram on p. 11; read the zones from the figure.

specConvert.title: Fuel conversion & high altitude
specConvert.html:
Shipped for natural gas only. Convert before the stove is installed; the kit is to be installed by an authorized service technician.

Pilot orifice#51 NG · #30 LP
Left / rear injector2.25 mm NG · 1.40 mm LP
Right / front injector#47 NG · 1.20 mm LP
Air shutter startNG 1/16" (1.5 mm) · LP 1/8" (3 mm) open

The kit also holds the regulator tower (labeled LP or NG) with 3 screws, Label A (back of the stove), Label B (rating plate) and a small fuel ID label for the valve. Propane also needs the baffle conversion: the secondary baffle comes off and is kept. Don't over-tighten the injectors. Finish with a leak check and a manometer pressure check.

High altitude (2000-4500 ft.)

Most gas suppliers derate gas above 2000 feet, so check first. If yours doesn't, install kit 157696 (NG) or 157695 (LP) with the injector steps above, and fill out and apply the high altitude label to the rating plate. Orifice sizes: NG Right/Front #44, Left/Rear #48; LP Right/Front 1.35 mm, Left/Rear 1.15 mm.

review.notes: Single US manual 139760: page headers read '139760_12 GF 500 DV 10/23' and the cover also carries '139760_G GF 500 DV 2/20'; unit.json lists revision 139760_13. Applies to serial numbers above 53003560. Ignition is a hand-lit continuous pilot (SIT Nova 820 millivolt valve, red piezo spark button); no electronic ignition or batteries in this manual. The optional remote (224910) has its own operating instructions, not included. The TOC and most internal cross-references are about one page off the physical pages (e.g. lighting 'p. 39' / 'inside back cover' = p. 35; maintenance 'p. 29' = p. 28; barrier parts 'fig. 56, page 31' = fig. 11.1 on p. 30; glass parts 'page 34' = p. 33); all pagerefs are physical pages. Shown only as figures and not transcribed: the dimensioned views (p. 4, dimensions not labelled in the text), the parallel/corner/alcove and mantel clearance drawings with lettered dimensions A-G (p. 9; the text doesn't tie each lettered set to a figure), the vent termination zone matrix (p. 11, text garbled), and log placement figures (p. 24). Pages 11, 12 and 19 have headers in a font offset by 29 code points ('NPVTSM_NO dc RMM as NMLOP' = '139760_12 GF 500 DV 10/23'). On p. 12 I decoded 'fnsulation oequirementW ^pply a minimum NLO”' as 'Insulation Requirement: Apply a minimum 1/2” thick foil-faced ceramic insulation blanket' behind the Snorkel (PN 225606), so the 1/2" thickness is printed as 'NLO' in the text. Other garbled figure labels on pp. 11-12 don't decode with that rule and were ignored. Horizontal terminal clearance table (p. 15): the Canada/U.S. column alignment of rows B, C, F, G and K is ambiguous in the extracted text, so the guide points to p. 15 instead of transcribing it. The p. 4 drawing pairs 25" with 535 mm and 30 1/8" with 785 mm, which don't match (p. 8 prints 25" (635 mm)); only p. 8 metric values are used. High altitude orifices (p. 20, 2000-4500 ft.) are larger than the sea-level ones on the Right/Front side and smaller on the Left/Rear side for both fuels (NG #44 vs #47, #48 vs 2.25 mm; LP 1.35 vs 1.20 mm, 1.15 vs 1.40 mm). Transcribed as printed, but worth confirming the left/right labels with Jøtul. The high altitude section cites ANSI Z21.88-2014 / CSA 2.33-2014 while the listing on p. 3 is to the 2019 editions and CAN/CGA 2.17-M17; the certification line uses p. 3. Warranty: Jøtul 'will repair or replace (including parts & labor)', but liability is later limited to the cost of a replacement component, excluding labor by others; the owner summary leaves out the labor claim. The glass gasket is called a 'ribbon gasket' on p. 28 and 'Gasket, Tadpole' on p. 33. Light-off over 4 seconds refers to a separate 'Ceramic Burner Guide' that isn't in this manual. The manual gives no blower electrical rating. Catalog checks: BTU inputs, P.4.1 efficiencies, millivolt ignition, optional blower and mobile-home approval all match. Weight (335 lb), heating area (2200 sq ft) and depth (23 in) aren't in the manual; the p. 4 drawing shows 30 1/8" and 28 1/2" (matching catalog height and width), but its dimensions aren't labelled in the text, so they aren't listed as checked. The catalog feature 'up to about 70% heat turn-down' isn't in the manual (it gives flame height adjustment of about 50% between LOW and HIGH; its 70% figure is the exhaust restrictor range).
